title: Leading an eleven-piece band and leaving Chicago
summary: His last Chicago job is with his own band at the Charleston Cafe; in November 1925 he hands it to Shirley Clay and heads to California over domestic problems.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The last job I had in Chicago was with my own band of eleven pieces. The Old Lincoln Gardens where Joe Oliver was playing burned down early in the year. It
was closed. They combined from the west side both the places; remodeled it and renamed it the Charleston Cafe.

It was there in mid October when I took my band after playing for several weeks. I suddenly told Shirley Clay, my second trumpet player, that I was quitting and going to California and I wanted him to take over the band. This is November, 1925.
What happened that you suddenly decided to come to California at that time, Mr. Blakeney?
